chain.title: The First Kitchen Tool
chain.desc: Craft a Flint Knife and try it on the appropriate harvests. Knives have special cutting and drop interactions; they are more than small swords.

chain.title: Give Ingredients a Place to Land
chain.desc: Build a Cutting Board. Place an ingredient on it and use the tool shown by its cutting recipe; not every recipe uses a knife.

chain.title: Save the Harvest's Fibers
chain.desc: Gather straw through knife harvesting and cutting recipes. Save it for canvas, rope and compost instead of throwing it away.

chain.title: A Useful Byproduct
chain.desc: Weave straw into canvas. This branch turns crop byproducts into practical furnishings and utility recipes.

chain.title: Support the Climbing Crops
chain.desc: Craft rope and try a tomato trellis or a safe climbing route. Rope is a utility branch rather than a compulsory ingredient in every meal.

chain.title: Strip Logs at the Board
chain.desc: Place a supported log on the Cutting Board and use an axe to obtain bark. The bark feeds the compost branch while the stripped log remains useful.

chain.title: Let the Compost Mature
chain.desc: Craft and place Organic Compost. Moisture and suitable nearby blocks help the compost mature into Rich Soil.

chain.title: A Better Foundation for Crops
chain.desc: Wait for placed compost to mature, then recover Rich Soil. Use it for the supported crop and farmland benefits rather than expecting an ordinary crafting-table recipe.

chain.title: Plant a Paddy
chain.desc: Find wild rice and establish a shallow-water paddy on suitable soil. Harvest the upper growth so the planted base can keep producing.

chain.title: Build a Tomato Patch
chain.desc: Gather tomato seeds and grow a crop. Once established, use rope to support taller tomato vines where the installed version allows it.

chain.title: A Crop That Replants Itself
chain.desc: Gather wild onions and replant some of the harvest. Keep a renewable supply for stews and feasts.

chain.title: Leaves for the Pantry
chain.desc: Establish a cabbage crop, then use the Cutting Board to prepare leaves for meals. Save seeds to expand the patch.

chain.title: A Reliable Kitchen Heat Source
chain.desc: Build and light a Stove. It can cook food directly and provide heat to the cooking equipment placed above it.

chain.title: Meals That Simmer Together
chain.desc: Place a Cooking Pot above an active heat source. Supply the recipe ingredients and any required serving container; output is collected from the pot.

chain.title: A Different Way to Cook
chain.desc: Make a Skillet and use it with an appropriate heat source. This is an alternative cooking branch, not a prerequisite for all pot recipes.

chain.title: Preserve the Tomato Harvest
chain.desc: Cook Tomato Sauce in the pot. Keep a supply for recipes that build a complete meal from prepared ingredients.

chain.title: Knead a Fresh Batch
chain.desc: Prepare Wheat Dough using an available recipe. Reserve part of the batch for bread and take the rest to the Cutting Board for pasta.

chain.title: Cut the Dough into Ribbons
chain.desc: Cut dough on the board with a knife to make Raw Pasta. Save some for a pot meal rather than cooking every ingredient separately.

chain.title: A Meal from Your Whole Kitchen
chain.desc: Prepare the meat and finish Pasta with Meatballs in the Cooking Pot. Your farming, cutting and simmering branches now supply one dish.

chain.title: Set Out a Feast
chain.desc: Cook a Stuffed Pumpkin with the installed ingredients and place it for serving. A feast block lets a shared kitchen feed several people.

chain.title: A Kitchen That Keeps Cooking
chain.desc: Grow replacement ingredients, prepare them at the board, and cook a fresh batch of meals from your own supply. Confirm once the kitchen has a repeatable food cycle.

content_revision: 2026-10-07: explicit branches, operational guidance, no collection filler

coverage.scope: A working kitchen, crop and compost branches, cutting-board processing, and shared feasts.
coverage.limitations: Recipe quantities, enabled content and progression settings may be changed by the installed pack.
coverage.verification_detail: Item models, entity language identifiers, dimension data, recipes and bundled guide text where present were inspected; this is data verification, not a Minecraft playthrough.

notes: Each requires list is intentional. Empty lists are independent entry routes. Links describe guided progression or demonstrated recipe/boss gates, not an assertion that every dependency is a game-enforced lock. Runtime scanning still filters unavailable items and entities.
